planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Profusion is a sterile, non-seeding chive selection bred to bloom heavily without becoming a self-sowing nuisance.

directions: Plant divisions in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Profusion produces an exceptionally heavy, long-lasting flush of pale purple pompom flowers over slender, mild-flavored leaves, without the risk of unwanted self-seeding that troubles many chive plantings, since the flowers are sterile and set no viable seed. Its extended bloom period makes it as valuable for pollinator gardens and cut-flower use as for the kitchen, and clumps stay tidy rather than spreading into surrounding beds. Harvest leaves regularly by snipping from the outer edge of the clump to encourage fresh, tender growth. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; closely related to garlic chives but distinguished by a sweeter fragrance and slightly narrower, keeled leaves.

directions: Sow seed or plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this East Asian species closely resembles garlic chives in flavor and use, its flat, garlic-scented leaves harvested fresh for the same culinary purposes, but its white, star-shaped flower umbels carry a notably sweeter fragrance that makes it a worthwhile addition to a pollinator or cutting bed as well as the herb garden. It spreads slowly by offsets into a dense clump and self-sows modestly in favorable conditions. Cut leaves at the base as needed through the growing season, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to keep plants vigorous.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; a Himalayan meadow species valued for true blue flowers, an unusual color in the onion family.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; Sikkim blue chives is a Himalayan meadow native prized for nodding umbels of true violet-blue, bell-shaped flowers in late summer, an unusually vivid and rare color within the onion genus. Its narrow, mild-flavored leaves are edible in the same way as common chives, though it is more often grown as a choice rock-garden or border ornamental for its flower color. It prefers slightly cooler, more evenly moist conditions than drought-tolerant ornamental alliums and benefits from a summer mulch in hot climates. Divide clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor and flowering.
